title: Yoav Waits for the Rain
summary: Yoav plants a tiny seed in a flowerpot and waits for it to grow. Grandma tells him that the Torah promises rain in its season when we walk in the good way, and Yoav discovers that he must care for his sprout every day too. A story about how small good deeds grow good things.
pages:
Grandma gives Yoav a tiny, tiny seed, brown and round.
"This is a lemon tree seed," she says.
Yoav looks at it. "It's so small!"

Yoav fills a flowerpot with soil.
He makes a little hole with his finger,
puts the seed inside and covers it up. "Good night, seed."

The next morning he runs to the flowerpot.
Nothing. Just brown soil.
"Grandma, it's not growing!"

"With a seed, you have to wait," says Grandma,
"and you have to take care of it every day:
a little water, a little sun, and lots of patience."

So every morning Yoav waters the flowerpot.
Every noon he moves it into the sun.
And every evening he tells it: "Grow, I'm waiting."

On Shabbat Grandma reads to him from the Chumash:
"If you walk in My laws... I will give you your rains in their season."
"What does that mean?" asks Yoav.

"God promises," says Grandma,
"that if we walk in the good way, the rain will come on time,
the trees will give fruit, and there will be peace in the land."

"Is the good way like how I take care of the seed?" asks Yoav.
"Exactly," Grandma smiles. "One small good deed, every day,
and it grows more and more good."

Then, one winter day, the sky fills with gray clouds.
Drip. Drip. Drip-drop.
The first rain is falling!

Yoav puts on his rain boots and runs outside.
He jumps in the puddles. Splash!
And his flowerpot stands in the rain and drinks.

And the next morning, in the brown soil,
there is a teeny-tiny green sprout with two leaves.
"Grandma! It's growing!" Yoav shouts. "Thank you, rain! Thank you, God!"

A small good deed is like a seed, too.
You water it every day, with patience and with love,
and one day, it will sprout and grow.
